holidays.name: World Lindy Hop Day
holidays.description: Swing dancers around the world celebrate the Lindy Hop, the joyful, high-energy partner dance known for swing-outs, improvised footwork and airborne moves. Dance studios, parks and ballrooms often host pop-up socials and open dance floors.
holidays.origin: The day honors the birthday of Frankie Manning, the Harlem dancer born on May 26, 1914. He is credited with helping popularize the Lindy Hop and with introducing its aerial moves. Dancers picked his birthday to celebrate the dance and its legacy.
holidays.funFact: The Lindy Hop grew out of 1920s and 1930s Harlem ballrooms like the Savoy. Its name is often linked to Charles Lindbergh's 1927 transatlantic 'hop'.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Cheesecake Day
holidays.description: This is a day to treat yourself to a creamy, tangy slice of cheesecake topped with juicy blueberries. Bakeries and dessert lovers mark it with swirls, compotes and no-bake versions.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a staple on food-holiday calendars for dessert fans.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries are one of the few fruits native to North America. Their deep blue color comes from anthocyanins, the same type of pigment found in red cabbage.

holidays.name: National Paper Airplane Day
holidays.description: Fold, crease and launch. This day celebrates the humble paper airplane, a pocket-sized aircraft that anyone can build in under a minute. It is an excuse to hold an office flight contest or fold a few jets with the kids.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a playful nod to one of the simplest and most popular DIY toys.
holidays.funFact: Paper airplane distance records are a serious business. A folded plane flown by a former American football player has been recorded flying over 69 meters (226 feet).
